subproblems.title: The open unit cube in Euclid k has Lebesgue measure 1 (reuse of the accepted cmcdtfrfg_cube_volume)
subproblems.statement: For every k ∈ ℕ, the open unit cube Q := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} of Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), with its Lebesgue measure (volume), has vol(Q) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ k : ℕ, volume {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the notation paragraph of the parent proof ("vol(Q₁) = 1", obtained from the measure-preserving coordinate map WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n → (Fin n → ℝ)), stated for every dimension k. Its exact Lean type is that of the already comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmcdtfrfg_cube_volume, which this split reuses; the parent and osc_exhaustion apply it with k = m + 1.

Notation. k ∈ ℕ; Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with volume = Lebesgue measure; y_i is the i-th coordinate of y; Q := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}.

1. Let ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ) be the coordinate map y ↦ (i ↦ y_i) (WithLp.ofLp), so (ofLp y) i = y_i for all i. By Mathlib's PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin k), ofLp is measure preserving from volume on Euclid k to volume on Fin k → ℝ, which is the product of the one-dimensional Lebesgue measures.
2. Let B := {w : Fin k → ℝ : w_i ∈ (0, 1) for all i} = Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1). B is measurable, being a product of measurable intervals (MeasurableSet.univ_pi with measurableSet_Ioo); in particular B is null-measurable.
3. Since y_i = (ofLp y) i, a point y ∈ Euclid k lies in Q if and only if ofLp y ∈ B. Hence Q = ofLp⁻¹(B) (extensionality and Set.mem_pi).
4. For a measure-preserving map the measure of the preimage of a null-measurable set equals the measure of the set (MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage). Hence vol(Q) = vol(ofLp⁻¹(B)) = vol(B).
5. By the product formula for open boxes (Real.volume_pi_Ioo), vol(B) = ∏_{i ∈ Fin k} ENNReal.ofReal(1 − 0) = ∏_{i ∈ Fin k} 1 = 1. For k = 0 the product is empty and also equals 1, so no case distinction is needed.
6. Combining steps 4 and 5, vol(Q) = 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: WithLp.ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ) is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp).
The cube is ofLp⁻¹ of the measurable box ∏_i (0, 1), so its volume equals the volume of the box.

subproblems.title: The double-integral oscillation on Q_δ passes to L¹ limits of continuous functions
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; fix δ ∈ ℝ with δ ≥ 0 and let Q_δ := {z ∈ Euclid n : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i} (Lebesgue measure). Let u : Euclid n → ℝ be integrable on Q₁, K ∈ ℝ, and let v_k : Euclid n → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) be continuous functions with ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy dx ≤ K for every k and ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0 as k → ∞. Then ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx ≤ K.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (v : ℕ → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (δ K : ℝ), IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → 0 ≤ δ → (∀ k, Continuous (v k)) → (∀ k, ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ∫ y in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, |v k x - v k y| ≤ K) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, |v k x - u x|) atTop (𝓝 0) → ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ∫ y in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, |u x - u y| ≤ K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof ("D(δ) ≤ D_k + vol(Q_δ)ε_k + vol(Q_δ)ε_k; letting k → ∞ gives D(δ) ≤ K₀V"), with the outputs of the sibling results smooth_approx and smooth_poincare replaced by the hypotheses on the continuous functions v_k (the parent supplies them), and with the integrability facts of step 1 of the parent proof written out for the set Q_δ.

Notation. n := m + 1; Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure vol; z_i is the i-th coordinate of z; S := Q_δ = {z : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}; Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}. μ := vol restricted to S, so ∫_S f = ∫ f dμ. All integrals are Bochner integrals, and every function to which linearity or monotonicity of the integral is applied below is first shown to be integrable.

1. S ⊆ Q₁. If z ∈ S then for every i, 0 ≤ δ < z_i and z_i < 1 − δ ≤ 1, because δ ≥ 0.
2. S lies in a compact ball. For z ∈ Q₁ every |z_i| < 1, so z_i² ≤ 1. Since ‖z‖ = √(Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} ‖z_i‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq) and ‖z_i‖² = z_i² (Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs), we get Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} z_i² ≤ Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} 1 = n (Finset.sum_le_sum) and hence ‖z‖ ≤ √n (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt). Hence S ⊆ Q₁ ⊆ B̄ := closedBall(0, √n). The ball B̄ is compact (Euclid n is finite dimensional, hence proper; isCompact_closedBall) and vol(B̄) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top), so vol(S) ≤ vol(B̄) < ∞.
3. Integrability. By step 2, μ is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). Put a := μ(univ) = vol(S), a real number ≥ 0. Since u is integrable on Q₁ ⊇ S, u ∈ L¹(μ) (IntegrableOn.mono_set). Each v_k is continuous, hence integrable on the compact set B̄ (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact) and therefore on S ⊆ B̄, so v_k ∈ L¹(μ). Consequently v_k − u, u − v_k and their absolute values lie in L¹(μ). Write ε_k := ∫_S |v_k − u| = ∫ |v_k − u| dμ; by hypothesis ε_k → 0.
4. Fubini integrability. Fix k. On the finite product measure μ ⊗ μ the functions (x, y) ↦ v_k(x) and (x, y) ↦ v_k(y) are integrable (Integrable.comp_fst and Integrable.comp_snd, which only need v_k ∈ L¹(μ) and μ finite). Hence G_k(x, y) := |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| is μ⊗μ-integrable, and by Fubini (Integrable.integral_prod_left) the function d_k(x) := ∫ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dμ(y) is μ-integrable. By definition ∫ d_k dμ = ∫_{x∈S}∫_{y∈S}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy dx, which is ≤ K by hypothesis.
5. Pointwise triangle inequality. For all x, y: u(x) − u(y) = (v_k(x) − v_k(y)) + (u(x) − v_k(x)) + (v_k(y) − u(y)), hence |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| + |u(x) − v_k(x)| + |v_k(y) − u(y)| (abs_add_three).
6. Inner integral. Fix x. The three functions of y on the right side of step 5 are μ-integrable: y ↦ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| (absolute value of a constant minus an L¹(μ) function; constants are μ-integrable because μ is finite), the constant y ↦ |u(x) − v_k(x)|, and y ↦ |v_k(y) − u(y)| (step 3). The left side y ↦ |u(x) − u(y)| is nonnegative. By monotonicity of the integral for a nonnegative function dominated by an integrable one (integral_mono_of_nonneg), linearity (integral_add) and ∫ b dμ = a·b for constants b (integral_const):
   h(x) := ∫ |u(x) − u(y)| dμ(y) ≤ d_k(x) + a·|u(x) − v_k(x)| + ε_k.
7. Outer integral. The right side of step 6, as a function of x, is μ-integrable (d_k by step 4, a·|u − v_k| by step 3, and a constant); the left side h(x) is nonnegative (integral_nonneg). Integrating step 6 over x with the same monotonicity and linearity (integral_const_mul for the middle term), and using ∫ |u − v_k| dμ = ∫ |v_k − u| dμ = ε_k (abs_sub_comm), we get
   D(u) := ∫_{x∈S}∫_{y∈S}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx = ∫ h dμ ≤ ∫ d_k dμ + a·ε_k + a·ε_k ≤ K + 2a·ε_k,
   the last step by step 4.
8. Limit. Since ε_k → 0, K + 2a·ε_k → K + 2a·0 = K (Tendsto.const_mul and Tendsto.add with tendsto_const_nhds). As D(u) ≤ K + 2a·ε_k for every k, passing to the limit (ge_of_tendsto') gives D(u) ≤ K. ∎
proof_key_steps: δ ≥ 0 gives Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ ⊆ closedBall(0, √(m + 1)); hence vol(Q_δ) < ∞, u ∈ L¹(Q_δ), and every continuous v_k ∈ L¹(Q_δ).
Fubini: (x, y) ↦ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| is integrable on Q_δ × Q_δ, so d_k(x) = ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy is integrable on Q_δ with ∫_{Q_δ} d_k ≤ K.
Integrating |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| + |u(x) − v_k(x)| + |v_k(y) − u(y)| in y and then in x gives D(u) ≤ K + 2 vol(Q_δ) ε_k with ε_k = ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u|.

subproblems.title: Exhausting the unit cube by the inner cubes Q_δ in the double-integral oscillation
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} and, for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {z ∈ Euclid n : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i} (Lebesgue measure). Let u : Euclid n → ℝ be integrable on Q₁ and K ∈ ℝ with ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx ≤ K for every δ ∈ (0, 1/2). Then ∫_{x∈Q₁}∫_{y∈Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx ≤ K.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (K : ℝ), IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → δ < 1 / 2 → ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ∫ y in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, |u x - u y| ≤ K) → ∫ x in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u x - u y| ≤ K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (δ_j := 1/(j + 3) ↓ 0 and dominated convergence, D(δ_j) → D(0)), carried out on the product Q₁ × Q₁, where the dominated convergence becomes continuity of the set integral along an increasing union. The integrability of |u(x) − u(y)| on Q₁ × Q₁ is step 1 of the parent proof.

Notation. n := m + 1; Euclid n with Lebesgue measure vol; z_i is the i-th coordinate of z; Q(δ) := {z : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}; Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; λ := vol ⊗ vol is the product measure on Euclid n × Euclid n (the volume of the product); F(x, y) := |u(x) − u(y)| ≥ 0. Sibling used: cube_volume (Submission.cmcdtfrfg_cube_volume) with k = m + 1, i.e. vol(Q₁) = 1.

1. The sequence δ_j. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 3) for j ∈ ℕ. Then 0 < δ_j ≤ 1/3 < 1/2; if j ≤ j' then δ_{j'} ≤ δ_j (one_div_le_one_div_of_le); and δ_j → 0, because j + 3 → +∞ (tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop, tendsto_atTop_add_const_right) and the reciprocal (j + 3)⁻¹ = 1/(j + 3) (one_div) of a sequence tending to +∞ tends to 0 (Filter.Tendsto.inv_tendsto_atTop).
2. The cubes Q_j := Q(δ_j). (a) Measurability: Q_j = ⋂_{i ∈ Fin n} ({z : δ_j < z_i} ∩ {z : z_i < 1 − δ_j}); every coordinate map z ↦ z_i is a continuous linear map (EuclideanSpace.proj i), hence measurable, so each of these sets is measurable (measurableSet_lt), and so is the intersection over the finite index set Fin n (MeasurableSet.iInter). (b) Monotonicity: if j ≤ j' and z ∈ Q_j, then δ_{j'} ≤ δ_j < z_i and z_i < 1 − δ_j ≤ 1 − δ_{j'} for all i, so Q_j ⊆ Q_{j'}. (c) Q_j ⊆ Q₁, because δ_j > 0 gives 0 < δ_j < z_i and z_i < 1 − δ_j < 1.
3. ⋃_j Q_j = Q₁. The inclusion ⊆ is step 2(c). Conversely let z ∈ Q₁. For each i we have z_i > 0 and 1 − z_i > 0; since δ_j → 0, eventually δ_j < z_i and eventually δ_j < 1 − z_i (Tendsto.eventually with gt_mem_nhds), i.e. eventually δ_j < z_i < 1 − δ_j. Because Fin n is finite, eventually these conditions hold for all i simultaneously (Filter.eventually_all), so some j satisfies z ∈ Q_j (Filter.Eventually.exists).
4. Integrability on Q₁ × Q₁. By cube_volume with k = m + 1, vol(Q₁) = 1 ≠ ∞, so ν := vol restricted to Q₁ is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict), and u ∈ L¹(ν) by hypothesis. The restriction of λ to Q₁ × Q₁ is ν ⊗ ν (Measure.prod_restrict). On ν ⊗ ν the functions (x, y) ↦ u(x) and (x, y) ↦ u(y) are integrable (Integrable.comp_fst and Integrable.comp_snd, ν finite), so F is ν⊗ν-integrable, i.e. F is λ-integrable on Q₁ × Q₁; hence F is also λ-integrable on every subset of Q₁ × Q₁ (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
5. Product sets. Let s_j := Q_j × Q_j. Each s_j is measurable (MeasurableSet.prod and step 2(a)); (s_j) is increasing (Set.prod_mono and step 2(b)); and since (Q_j) is increasing, ⋃_j (Q_j × Q_j) = (⋃_j Q_j) × (⋃_j Q_j) (Set.iUnion_prod_of_monotone: a pair with x ∈ Q_a and y ∈ Q_b lies in Q_{max(a,b)} × Q_{max(a,b)}), which equals Q₁ × Q₁ by step 3.
6. Convergence. F is λ-integrable on ⋃_j s_j = Q₁ × Q₁ (steps 4 and 5), and the s_j are measurable and increasing, so ∫_{s_j} F dλ → ∫_{Q₁×Q₁} F dλ (tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone). This is exactly the dominated convergence of the parent's step 3: 1_{s_j}F → 1_{Q₁×Q₁}F pointwise, dominated by the integrable function 1_{Q₁×Q₁}F.
7. Fubini identification. For each j, F is λ-integrable on s_j ⊆ Q₁ × Q₁ (step 4), so Fubini's theorem for set integrals (setIntegral_prod) gives ∫_{s_j} F dλ = ∫_{x∈Q_j}∫_{y∈Q_j}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx =: D_j. Likewise ∫_{Q₁×Q₁} F dλ = ∫_{x∈Q₁}∫_{y∈Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx =: D. By step 6, D_j → D.
8. Conclusion. Each δ_j lies in (0, 1/2) (step 1), so the hypothesis with δ = δ_j gives D_j ≤ K for every j. A limit of real numbers that are all ≤ K is ≤ K (le_of_tendsto'), hence D ≤ K, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: δ_j := 1/(j + 3) ∈ (0, 1/2) decreases to 0; the cubes Q_j := Q_{δ_j} are measurable, increasing, contained in Q₁, and their union is Q₁.
By cube_volume (k = m + 1), vol(Q₁) = 1, so |u(x) − u(y)| is integrable on Q₁ × Q₁ for vol ⊗ vol (Measure.prod_restrict, Integrable.comp_fst, Integrable.comp_snd).
The products Q_j × Q_j increase to Q₁ × Q₁; tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone and setIntegral_prod give D(δ_j) → D(Q₁).
D(δ_j) ≤ K for every j, so D(Q₁) ≤ K.

subproblems.title: Mean deviation is bounded by the double-integral oscillation on a set of volume 1
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, let S ⊆ Euclid (m + 1) be any set with Lebesgue measure vol(S) = 1, and let u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ be integrable on S. Then, with c := ∫_S u, ∫_{x∈S}|u(x) − c| dx ≤ ∫_{x∈S}∫_{y∈S}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), volume S = 1 → IntegrableOn u S → ∫ x in S, |u x - ∫ y in S, u y| ≤ ∫ x in S, ∫ y in S, |u x - u y|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (c := ∫_{Q₁}u; since vol(Q₁) = 1, u(x) − c = ∫_{Q₁}(u(x) − u(y)) dy, hence |u(x) − c| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| dy = h_0(x); integrate over Q₁), stated for an arbitrary set S of volume 1. The integrability of the inner integral h is step 1 of the parent proof.

Notation. Euclid (m + 1) with Lebesgue measure vol. μ := vol restricted to S (Measure.restrict is defined for every set S). Integrals ∫ … dμ are exactly the set integrals ∫_S … of the statement. c := ∫ u dμ = ∫_S u.

1. μ is a probability measure: μ(univ) = vol(S) = 1 (Measure.restrict_apply_univ, valid for every set S). In particular μ is finite, constants are μ-integrable, and ∫ b dμ = μ(univ)·b = b for every constant b (integral_const). By hypothesis u ∈ L¹(μ).
2. Integrability on the product. On μ ⊗ μ the functions (x, y) ↦ u(x) and (x, y) ↦ u(y) are integrable (Integrable.comp_fst and Integrable.comp_snd, using that μ is finite). Hence F(x, y) := |u(x) − u(y)| is μ⊗μ-integrable (difference, then absolute value), and by Fubini (Integrable.integral_prod_left) h(x) := ∫ |u(x) − u(y)| dμ(y) is a μ-integrable function of x.
3. Pointwise bound. Fix x. The function y ↦ u(x) − u(y) is μ-integrable (a constant minus u), and by linearity (integral_sub) and step 1, ∫ (u(x) − u(y)) dμ(y) = u(x) − ∫ u dμ = u(x) − c. Hence |u(x) − c| = |∫ (u(x) − u(y)) dμ(y)| ≤ ∫ |u(x) − u(y)| dμ(y) = h(x), because the absolute value of an integral is at most the integral of the absolute value (abs_integral_le_integral_abs).
4. Integration. The function x ↦ |u(x) − c| is nonnegative and pointwise ≤ h(x), and h is μ-integrable by step 2. By monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono_of_nonneg: nonnegative left side, integrable right side, pointwise inequality), ∫ |u(x) − c| dμ(x) ≤ ∫ h dμ = ∫_{x∈S}∫_{y∈S}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx. With c = ∫_S u this is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ := vol restricted to S has μ(univ) = vol(S) = 1, so it is a probability measure and u ∈ L¹(μ).
Fubini: |u(x) − u(y)| is μ⊗μ-integrable, so h(x) := ∫_S|u(x) − u(y)| dy is integrable on S.
Since μ(univ) = 1, u(x) − ∫_S u = ∫_S (u(x) − u(y)) dy, hence |u(x) − ∫_S u| ≤ h(x).
Integrating the nonnegative function |u − ∫_S u| ≤ h over S gives ∫_S|u − ∫_S u| ≤ ∫_S∫_S|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx.
